newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dehaene-EMU choice easier if countries near 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dehaene-EMU choice easier if countries near 3 pct.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said in a radio interview on Wednesday it would make it easier in deciding which countries can join a single currency if governments respect the Maastricht treaty target limiting budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product.
"Even if the treaty leaves soom room, the nearer we get to the three percent, the less discussion there will be," he told French radio.
It was up to all countries to put their own public finances in order ahead of the decision due in April/May next year on which countries qualify for European monetary union.
France's new Socialist-led government has said it does not expect to reduce its public deficit to precisely 3.0 percent of GDP this year.
It says it wants to use provisions in the Maastricht treaty which take into account a falling trend in deficits towards three percent of GDP.
